slots.title: Treatment of component PPV/PPA responses in blast-vibration literature
slots.instruction: Review how blast-vibration literature treats component PPV and PPA responses: whether they are modelled separately by component (e.g., transverse, vertical, longitudinal), jointly as correlated responses, or summarised through vector or resultant peak quantities. Write in flowing paragraphs.

slots.title: Methods for multivariate or constrained response prediction
slots.instruction: Identify the methods and diagnostics used for multivariate or constrained response prediction when blast vibration components are correlated or linked by a vector quantity. Write in flowing paragraphs.

slots.title: Literature precedent for component-peak scaling of recorded time histories
slots.instruction: Assess whether the blast-vibration literature contains precedents for scaling recorded blast vibration time histories to match predicted component peak accelerations or velocities. Write in flowing paragraphs.

slots.title: Description of scenario scaling to distinguish from related methods
slots.instruction: Determine how scenario scaling of recorded blast time histories to predicted component peaks should be characterised so that it is not confused with spectral matching, target-spectrum adjustment, or synthetic blast waveform simulation. Write in flowing paragraphs.

slots.title: Limitations of peak-component scaling relative to physics-based source models
slots.instruction: Identify the limitations that should be stated when scenario waveforms are scaled by peak component response rather than generated from a physics-based blast source model. Write in flowing paragraphs.

constraints: The output is written in English.
Scope is restricted to blast-vibration literature; generic scaled-distance attenuation overviews that do not address the component-wise or multivariate modelling gap are outside scope.
The subject is component-wise responses (PPV and PPA by axis), not resultant or vector peak quantities alone.
